environment: Queensland community solar and battery projects keep pushing the state closer to its renewable energy targets
Reef Check volunteers report encouraging signs of coral recovery on parts of the Great Barrier Reef this spring
science: Australian researchers make progress on new marine and medical science breakthroughs supporting reef and human health
sports: Queensland teams gear up for a huge September as NRL and AFL finals footy hits fever pitch
stories.overview: A gentle spring awakening across the Sunshine State, from clearer reef waters to footy finals fever, reminds us why Queenslanders reckon they live in the best place on earth

segments.title: The Open
segments.script: G'day and welcome to ParkSyde Bright Side, I'm Alex Mercer, and mate, it is a ripper of a Friday out there. September the eleventh, footy finals are heating up, the reef's looking chirpier, and there's actual good news to talk about for once. I'm Jamie, and I reckon Fridays like this are exactly why we do this show. We've got environment wins, a bit of science that'll make you go huh that's neat, sport, and Sam's got the weather sorted for the weekend. Grab your cuppa, settle in, we'll try not to bore you too much. Let's kick things off with some genuinely nice environment news out of our own backyard.

segments.title: Green Desk
segments.script: So Alex, Queensland's renewable rollout keeps chugging along nicely, more rooftop solar, more community batteries popping up in suburbs from Brisbane to Cairns. It's the unglamorous kind of good news, nobody's throwing a parade, but the numbers keep climbing. Yeah and it's not just the big flashy wind farms either, it's your neighbour with panels on the roof and a battery in the shed quietly doing their bit. Every little bit of sunshine harvested is one less coal fired kilowatt, and let's be honest, Queensland's never been short on sunshine. Speaking of things looking up, Reef Check volunteers have been out snorkelling around parts of the Great Barrier Reef and reporting some genuinely encouraging coral recovery. It's not mission accomplished by any stretch, but healthier patches of coral popping back to life is exactly the kind of quietly hopeful news we love bringing you.

segments.title: Science & Tomorrow
segments.script: Right, science time, and I promise to try and keep up, Jamie. Aussie researchers have been chipping away at some genuinely clever marine and medical science, the kind of work that quietly makes life better without ever making the front page. That's the thing about good science, it rarely comes with fireworks, it comes with years of patient lab work and then suddenly a breakthrough that helps protect the reef or improve someone's health. Slow and steady really does win the race sometimes. Feels like half of Australia's best scientists are quietly beavering away in labs right now while we're all worrying about footy tipping. Good on them, someone's got to keep the smart people employed.

segments.title: Weather
segments.script: Cheers Alex, g'day everyone, Sam here with your southeast Queensland outlook. We're firmly into spring mode now, expect plenty of sunshine across Brisbane, the Gold Coast and the Sunshine Coast, with daytime temps sitting comfortably in the low to mid twenties. Overnight will still carry a bit of a bite, so don't packed away the doona just yet, but by lunchtime it'll feel glorious for a walk along the river or the beach. There's a light onshore breeze expected through the weekend, keeping things fresh without any real chance of rain spoiling your footy finals plans. All in all, it's shaping up to be a cracker of a weekend to be outdoors, so get out there and enjoy it while the humidity's still behaving itself. Back to you Alex and Jamie.

segments.title: The Scoreboard
segments.script: Righto, footy time, and mate, September is when things get properly serious. NRL and AFL finals are firing up, and there's a genuine buzz around Queensland with our teams still very much in the mix. There's nothing quite like finals footy weather isn't there, everyone's suddenly an expert, the barbecues are firing, and half of Queensland's got an opinion on the ref. It's basically a second season of good vibes on top of the actual footy. Couldn't agree more, whatever happens on the field, it's bringing people together in pubs and loungerooms right across the state. That's the real prize if you ask me, well, that and the actual trophy I suppose.

segments.title: Overview & Outro
segments.script: Well that's about it for us today, thanks for spending your Friday with us here at ParkSyde Bright Side. Good news out there if you go looking for it, the reef's recovering, the sun's shining, and the footy's got everyone talking. It really has been a lovely one to bring you today, and Sam's forecast means there's zero excuse not to get outside this weekend. Go find a bit of sunshine, maybe even plant something while you're at it. Big thanks to Sam for the weather, and to all of you tuning in, we don't take it for granted. Keep an eye on the environment, keep backing the science, and keep cheering on your footy team, whoever they may be. We'll be back tomorrow with more of the good stuff, because Queensland's always got a bright side worth talking about. Until then, look after yourselves and each other. That's a wrap from ParkSyde Bright Side, I'm Alex Mercer, alongside Jamie, have a ripper weekend everyone, and we'll catch you next time.
